meta.description: Multi-pathogen profile definitions for concurrent simulation
meta.notes: Each pathogen runs as an independent instance with separate mass pools per room. Profiles can be activated at initiation or introduced mid-cruise via 'introduction_epoch'.

pathogens.name: Norwalk Virus (Norovirus GII.4)

observation_model.evidence_grade: C - declared observation process, not identified (#27)
observation_model.notes: Every number in this block is a declared assumption, class C, origin Tr: the three severity vectors are Table 2 and section 4.1 of docs/norovirus/cruise_pathogen_severity_observation_priors_v2.md, which grades each entry [A] (assumed prior) and states that the decomposition is not identified by the one cruise investigation behind it - many severity-specific vectors give the same weighted fraction. That one aggregate is anchor A3, which is why A3 no longer scores (#23). Consequence, stated rather than repaired: the reported-attack-rate comparison against VSP is CONDITIONAL on this assumed observation process, and agreement with a reported rate is not evidence that these fifteen numbers are right. No entry was chosen against A1, A2, A3, A5 or any VSP quantity. Uncertainty is carried by prior.scenarios as whole coherent vectors, never by sweeping components independently, per section 8 of the same document: independent component sweeps produce reporting ladders no observer could exhibit. lab_sampling_probability_by_severity is operational rather than biological (section 9 there) and moves lab-confirmed counts only, not the VSP reported rate; it stays a declared axis. episode_reporting_window_days 2.0 is the illness duration the vectors were elicited over (uncomplicated norovirus 1-3 days), also declared.

base_reporting.source: priors v2 Table 2 and section 4.1: the shipped decomposition, weighted eligible-case reporting about 0.61 against the 0.60 [E] aggregate. Class C, origin Tr. Not identified by that aggregate.

isolation_avoidance_post_recognition.source: priors v2 section 4.1, stated verbatim there: anticipated cabin isolation suppresses subclinical and mild presentation after outbreak recognition while moderate and severe cases stay hard to conceal. Class C, origin Tr. Direction is argued in the source; magnitude is declared.

incubation.notes: Pooled norovirus GII: mu 0.182, sigma 0.445 (median 1.2 d, GSD 1.56, 95% 0.5-2.9 d) from Lee et al. 2013 via docs/ctb_incubation_spec.md - GII rather than the GI the pathogen_id implies, because this profile's genotypes are GII.4/GII.17/GII.2, and the spec finds no genotype-specific fits within GII. Dose term dose_shift 0.12 / floor 0.3 from the spec. dose_reference_log10 is this profile's own beta-Poisson N50 (16871 particles, alpha 0.111 / beta 32.81), not the spec's 18, which this note previously mislabelled as RT-PCR units: Teunis's 18 is a disaggregated-virus figure whose unit is contested in print, the fitted pair's own dose axis is administered genome copies, and neither is an RT-PCR unit (docs/literature/consensus_tranche_23_teunis_atmar_dose_unit.md). acquired_particles is in model units whose commensurability with genome copies is not established, so referencing the literature assay unit would put every simulated host on the dose floor and turn a conditioning term into a constant. Consequence: a typical (near-ID50) host presents at the literature median, and the dose effect is anchored in direction but not calibrated in magnitude. host_factors omitted deliberately: the spec finds no literature support for a frailty effect on incubation, so it stays a sensitivity arm.

strain_evolution.notes: Rates from docs/paper3/variant_surveillance_spec.md §1.3. superinfection_susceptibility and recombination_rate are placeholders pending a literature anchor (docs/paper3/variant_surveillance_plan.md §7). immune_waning: refractory_days 56 and half_life_days 1095 are anchored on homotypic challenge protection lasting at least months and modelled immunity duration of 4.1-8.7 years (Simmons et al., Emerg Infect Dis 2013); the homotypic HR 0.39 of Ford-Siltz et al. (Clin Infect Dis 2020) is a multi-year hazard ratio, not a per-epoch susceptibility. Both are sensitivity axes. refractory_protection is applied as a per-epoch hazard reduction, so any value below 1.0 leaks at that rate every hour: 1.0 makes within-window re-infection escape-only, which is the intended contract.

sequencing_assay.notes: Assay design from docs/paper3/variant_surveillance_spec.md §2.1. read_accuracy is per-read consensus accuracy for this amplicon; read depth and the reporting floor are operator dials set at run time, not pathogen properties.

pathogens.presymptomatic_shedding_notes: Atmar et al., Emerg Infect Dis 2008: virus was first detected in stool at a median approximately 36 hours post-challenge, essentially concurrent with symptom onset; 0.5 days is the generous presymptomatic window.

pathogens.name: SARS-CoV-2 (Respiratory)
pathogens.asymptomatic_shedding_notes: Equal to shedding_curve_log10: no symptom-conditioned offset is claimed on this arm. The shipped curve carried a 1.0-1.5 log10 offset below the symptomatic peak with no source, and it is REFUTED - measured upper-respiratory viral loads are similar between symptomatic and asymptomatic people through the first week (docs/literature/mql_tranche_9_sars_cov2.md, corroborated in docs/literature/edison_covid_influenza_bundle_review.md). Removing it is #31's action on the register's asymptomatic_shedding_log10 row. Equality is the null, not a claim that the two curves are identical past week one, where the measurements thin out; a separate asymptomatic curve returns only with a measurement to put in it.
pathogens.symptomatic_fraction_notes: 0.69 = 1 - 0.31, the asymptomatic share among people found by SCREENING rather than by symptoms, Buitrago-Garcia 2020 (PLoS Med 17(9):e1003346), Grade B. Screened is the right denominator because a symptom-based denominator conditions on the outcome being measured. Sah 2021's 35.1% (PNAS 118(34):e2109229118) is the alternative and is a declared scenario axis, giving 0.649. This replaces illness_probability eta 0.4 / gamma 0.12, deleted as unattributed near-neighbours of norovirus's Korkin pair: the Hill form is strictly increasing in dose and no dose-conditional presentation measurement exists for SARS-CoV-2, so the arm carries a measured proportion instead, as influenza_a does after Carrat.

severity_model.evidence_grade: B for the age ladder (Herrera-Esposito 2022) and the asymptomatic share (Buitrago-Garcia 2020); C for the band-to-decade mapping and the declared subclinical null
severity_model.notes: Age-conditioned, and the age dependence is the sourced part. Herrera-Esposito & de los Campos 2022 (BMC Infect Dis 22:311, DOI 10.1186/s12879-022-07262-0) estimate infection-severe (ISR) and infection-critical (ICR) rates by age decade from multi-country seroprevalence studies, Grade B: ISR 0.103% (0-9) to 30.3% (80+), ICR 0.0088% to 19.4%, age-logistic slopes 0.076 and 0.099 per year. Those rates are denominated in INFECTIONS, which is the denominator these five states use, so moderate = ISR - ICR (severe, not critical) and severe_critical = ICR read straight off that table. Wiersinga 2020's 81%/14%/5% mild/severe/critical ladder is NOT used numerically: its denominator is diagnosed cases, and its hospitalised shares exceed the infection-denominated rates by more than an order, so importing it would silently change the denominator. Tabata and every other Diamond Princess severity report is BARRED here - Diamond Princess is Track D's training hull, and severity read off it would make the held-out score circular. asymptomatic 0.31 is the screened denominator of Buitrago-Garcia 2020 (PLoS Med 17(9):e1003346), matching symptomatic_fraction 0.69; Sah 2021's 35.1% is the alternative denominator and is the declared axis for it, not an average taken with it. Declared, not measured, and marked as such: (1) subclinical is 0.0 because no source separates a subclinical rung from mild on this arm, and a null is the honest entry rather than an invented split - mild therefore carries the whole non-hospitalised symptomatic mass; (2) each band reads the decade containing its midpoint, an open-ended band taking its lower bound plus five years, because no population config in this repository states a numeric span for its named bands or an age distribution inside any band; (3) child, young_adult, adult, middle_aged and senior are read as 5-17, 18-34, 35-49, 50-64 and 65+, which the picard population config leaves unstated; (4) base_probabilities is a fallback for a band this block does not name, set to the adult vector so an unnamed band reads a mid-range case mix rather than either tail - it is not a population average and carries no evidential claim. Cruise passengers are not a general population (Pavli's measured mean passenger age is 72.6), which is why the ladder reads the agent's age instead of one vector. No entry was chosen against Diamond Princess, Greg Mortimer, Willebrand or any attack rate Track D scores.

active_screening.notes: Off, so the arm's baseline is passive ascertainment. The Diamond Princess daily campaign and Greg Mortimer's ship-wide test event are case-finding campaigns that reach hosts who never presented; they are represented by enabling this in the #33 scenarios, never by widening the sampling vector.

observation_model.evidence_grade: B for the PCR sensitivity anchors (Kucirka 2020); C for the declared reporting and sampling vectors and for the interpolation between anchors
observation_model.notes: Two observables, kept apart: symptom onset (a dated presentation) and a PCR positive (a specimen plus an assay). Track D scores COVID on confirmed cases and onset dates, so neither may be read off truth state, and the sick-call hazard the syndromic modality applies to norovirus is NOT this arm's ascertainment channel. The three severity vectors are declared, class C, and are the arm's declared axis: eligibility 0 on the two rungs that never present, 1 on mild and above because a dated onset needs only symptoms; passive reporting rises with severity and rises again once an outbreak is recognised. They are not set to reproduce any Diamond Princess or Greg Mortimer count - the campaigns those hulls ran are active screening, added as scenarios in #33, and active_screening is off here so the profile's own baseline is passive infirmary ascertainment. assay_sensitivity_by_time_since_infection is sourced: Kucirka 2020 (Ann Intern Med 173(4):262, DOI 10.7326/M20-1495) reports RT-PCR false-negative rates by day since exposure - 100% on day 1, 67% on day 4, 38% on day 5, a minimum of 20% on day 8, rising to 66% on day 21 - inverted to sensitivity here and linearly interpolated between those five reported days, which is the declared part. Grade B for the anchors, C for the interpolation. The curve is indexed by days since INFECTION and its last entry is held, like a shedding curve. Detectability and infectiousness stay on separate clocks: shedding_duration_days 15 is upper-respiratory RNA positivity, culture positivity ends far earlier, and this curve moves only whether a specimen tests positive. episode_reporting_window_days 7.0 is recovery_day, declared. Fatality is not modelled on this arm, so no IFR ladder is declared here; Levin 2020's age-specific IFR is recorded in the register and enters nothing.

pathogens.shedding_duration_notes: Separated from recovery_day 7 so clinical resolution does not end shedding, the defect fixed for norovirus in #43 (#51). The curve is a nasal RNA concentration and this arm is scored on PCR detectability, so the clock carries the upper-respiratory RNA-positivity duration, not the infectious one: Cevik 2020 (10.1016/S2666-5247(20)30172-5; meta-analysis of 43 studies, 3229 individuals) pooled mean 17.0 d (95% CI 15.5-18.6), Fontana 2020 (10.1017/ice.2020.1273; 28 studies) pooled median 18.4 d (15.5-21.3), Wu 2023 (10.1016/j.ijid.2023.02.011; Omicron meta-analysis) mean PCR positivity 10.82 d (10.23-11.42). Interval [10.8, 18.4]; 15 is the authored curve's own length and within 0.4 d of the interval midpoint (14.6), chosen for neither anchor. Grade B, Origin R. Viable-virus duration is much shorter (no culture past day 9 of illness in Cevik's review; 5.16 d for Omicron, 4.18-6.14, Wu 2023; culture positivity 83/52/13.5/8% at days 5/7/10/14, Keske 2023), so the tail days 8-14 overstate infectious emission by the 0.02% of curve mass they carry; a separate infectious-duration field is not added here.

incubation.notes: SARS-CoV-2 ancestral: mu 1.758, sigma 0.450 (median 5.8 d, GSD 1.57, 95% 2.3-14.6 d) from Wei et al. 2021 via docs/ctb_incubation_spec.md. Later lineages incubate faster (Omicron median 3.5 d, mu 1.253 / sigma 0.400): set median_days per scenario rather than treating 5.8 as current. Dose term dose_shift 0.15 / floor 0.3 from the spec, referenced to this profile's own beta-Poisson N50 (2670 particles, alpha 0.18 / beta 58) rather than the spec's TCID50 figure, for the model-unit reason given on norwalk_gi.

strain_evolution.notes: Rates from docs/paper3/variant_surveillance_spec.md §1.3. superinfection_susceptibility and recombination_rate are placeholders pending a literature anchor (docs/paper3/variant_surveillance_plan.md §7). immune_waning: refractory_days 90 follows the 90-day reinfection convention; half_life_days 180 reflects rapid waning of protection against infection, with a small residual. Sensitivity axis. refractory_protection is applied as a per-epoch hazard reduction, so any value below 1.0 leaks at that rate every hour: 1.0 makes within-window re-infection escape-only, which is the intended contract.

sequencing_assay.notes: Assay design from docs/paper3/variant_surveillance_spec.md §2.1. read_accuracy is per-read consensus accuracy for this amplicon; read depth and the reporting floor are operator dials set at run time, not pathogen properties.

pathogens.presymptomatic_shedding_notes: He et al., Nat Med 2020: infectiousness begins approximately 2.3 days before symptom onset; 2.0 days is the profile window.

pathogens.name: Influenza A (pooled)
pathogens.notes: Pooled influenza A: no subtype-specific biology. The Edison bundle's H1N1/H3N2 strain table, base_susceptibility 0.65, dose_adjustment, surface_deposition_fraction and share-valued transmission_route_weights are deliberately not carried over; see docs/parameter_provenance_register.md section 3.3 for why each is refused, and docs/proposals/influenza_arm_activation_plan.md for the activation sequence. Scored rungs are MAARI and NAT-confirmed infection, kept separate.
pathogens.presymptomatic_shedding_notes: Ip et al., Clin Infect Dis 2017: shedding begins approximately 1 day before symptom onset; 1.0 day is the profile window.
pathogens.environmental_release_notes: Level, not shape. Emission is 10^(curve - this value) per day, converted to the epoch by SimClock, so 0.82 sets the symptomatic peak (curve 7.2) to 10^6.38 = 2.4e6 copies per day, which is Yan 2018 (EMIT, PNAS 115:1081, DOI 10.1073/pnas.1716561115) exhaled geometric means 3.8e4 fine + 1.2e4 coarse copies per 30-min sample extrapolated to 24 h. Grade C: the measurement is exhaled breath in a clinical facility, and Yan finds exhaled load uncorrelated with NP swab load, so the nasal-indexed curve supplies only the temporal shape while the level is pinned to a measured exhaled rate. Excludes hand contamination and large-droplet spray, so it is a lower bound on total release. Declared, and selected against no anchor.
pathogens.airborne_emission_notes: Fine (<=5 um) share of exhaled emission, 3.8e4 / (3.8e4 + 1.2e4) = 0.76 from the same Yan 2018 paired measurement. The coarse remainder deposits near the source, which is what the fomite route draws on. Replaces the Edison bundle's surface_deposition_fraction 1e-3, which was the deprecated alias of this key with no stated referent. Sourced interval [0.76, 0.92], grade B (#42, literature tranche 27): the floor is Yan 2018's own ratio, the ceiling is Chow 2023's fine load ~12x coarse, and Coleman 2021's SARS-CoV-2 0.85 falls inside. Dimensionless only because this arm's level is a measured exhaled rate rather than a specimen titre; the scalar ships at the interval floor and #36 sweeps the span.

severity_model.evidence_grade: B for the two rungs Carrat measures, P for the splits inside them
severity_model.notes: Carrat 2008 (DOI 10.1093/aje/kwm375) fixes two rungs: any symptoms 66.9% of infections, so asymptomatic + subclinical = 0.331; lower-respiratory symptoms 21.0% of infections, read as moderate or worse. Mild = 0.669 - 0.210 = 0.459 is then implied. The two splits inside those rungs (asymptomatic vs subclinical 0.200/0.131, moderate vs severe_critical 0.200/0.010) are declared, not measured, and are swept. No value here was chosen against Ward 2010 or Millman 2015.

active_screening.notes: Off by default, which makes the arm's baseline passive infirmary ascertainment. Ward 2010's research testing of a whole voyage is represented by enabling this and raising selection_probability_per_day, not by widening the sampling vector below: a case-finding campaign reaches symptomatic hosts who never presented, and passive sampling cannot.

observation_model.notes: Every number here is declared and swept, because the arm's candidate anchors are themselves observation-layer quantities: setting these to reproduce Ward's 0.7% presenting or Millman's 3.7%/6.2% MAARI would make those anchors unfalsifiable. Recorded for comparison rather than calibration: these values imply a pre-recognition medically-attended fraction near 0.16 per infection against the roughly 0.08 Ward measures on one voyage (0.7% presenting against 8.9% NAT-confirmed), so the arm starts about 2x too visible and closing that is the sweep's job. assay_sensitivity 0.95 is RT-PCR on an adequate NP specimen (Grade C), kept separate from the sampling vector so that detection-technology scenarios move sensitivity without moving clinical behaviour.

incubation.notes: Human influenza A: mu 0.336, sigma 0.412 (median 1.4 d, GSD 1.51) from Lessler et al. 2009 via docs/ctb_incubation_spec.md, truncated 0.5-7.0 d to match the tng_shipboard_influenza analogue that already carries this same kernel as a shape. Dose terms dose_shift 0.10 / floor 0.4 from the spec. dose_reference_log10 0.59 is this profile's own exponential-model N50 (ln(2)/k = 0.693/0.18 = 3.85 particles), the exponential analogue of the beta-Poisson N50 convention documented on norwalk_gi in active_profiles.json: acquired_particles is in model units, so referencing a literature TCID50 or EID50 figure would put every simulated host on the dose floor and turn a conditioning term into a constant. Consequence: a near-ID50 host presents at the literature median, and the dose effect is anchored in direction but not calibrated in magnitude. host_factors omitted, as on the shipped profiles.

pathogens.shedding_duration_notes: Separated from recovery_day 5 so clinical resolution does not end shedding, the defect fixed for norovirus in #43. Seven days spans Carrat 2008's reported shedding through about day 5 plus Ip 2017's presymptomatic day; the 15-value curve's tail beyond it contributes under 1% of the linear-scale integral.
pathogens.base_susceptibility_notes: Deliberately 1.0, not the Edison bundle's 0.65. Prior immunity is a per-season, subtype- and age-conditioned scenario input: on Ward's single voyage pdm09 ran at RR 17.4 in children 3-6 with zero cases over 65 while H3N2 was flat across every age band, so no scalar represents it. It is declared on the manifest and swept, never fitted here.

sequencing_assay.notes: Assay design from docs/paper3/variant_surveillance_spec.md §2.1. read_accuracy is per-read consensus accuracy for this amplicon; read depth and the reporting floor are operator dials set at run time, not pathogen properties.
